copies.headline: Adam Is Boring Again, And Unbeatable
copies.body: Adam leads the league at 139.4 a game, owns a 78-32 all-play, and sits at -0.1 luck — nobody handed him anything. The 89 draft grade was T-2nd on the cabin floor and it's aged like it should: Jayden Daniels, Kenneth Walker III, Bucky Irving, and a roster that still projects 134 a week, best in the league. The only wobble is recent — 108.9, 106.1 around a 170.8 spike, 48% all-play over three weeks. That's the defending champ with a 7-3 record and nothing actually wrong. Kaleb's next.

copies.headline: 5-5 Is A Lie Christian Keeps Living
copies.body: Christian is 5-5 and it's fiction. The all-play says 70-40, T-2nd of 12, and the luck column says -1.4 wins — he's been scoring like a contender and collecting participation trophies. 127.2 a game, 3rd of 12. Last three weeks: 123.5, 110.4, 149.9, an all-play of 24-9 that's T-1st of 12, and a W3 streak to show for it. The draft was real too, 89 out of 100, T-2nd of 12. CeeDee Lamb and George Kittle project 130 against John in Week 11. The record will correct itself.

copies.headline: Logan's 4-6 Is A Clerical Error
copies.body: Logan is 4-6 with an all-play record of 66-44, 60% and 4th of 12 — that's not a bad team, that's a team getting mugged weekly. The luck number says it plainly: -2.0 wins below expected, 12th-luckiest of 12, with 1310.5 points against, the most anyone has absorbed. He's scored 146.4, 130.4 and 117.8 the last three weeks and went 22-11 all-play for it. Justin Jefferson, Joe Burrow and a roster index of 75 say the floor is real. The dress he wore for 2025 was earned. This one wouldn't be.

copies.headline: John Scores Like a Contender, Loses Like Everyone Else
copies.body: John is 5-5 with the 2nd-best scoring average in the league at 130.1 a game and an all-play record of 70-40, T-2nd of 12. That is a very good team wearing a .500 costume, and the minus-1.4 luck confirms it. The problem is the trend: 165.1, then 126.8, then 110.2, which is a slide, not a blip. The roster projects 117 a week, 8th of 12, and outside Trey McBride and Tee Higgins it thins out fast. Week 11 against Christian, 121 projected. Beat somebody, John.

copies.headline: Isaac's Roster Finally Caught Up To Him
copies.body: Isaac has spent ten weeks looking like a 110.7-per-game team, 10th of 12 in scoring, with a 49-61 all-play that puts him 7th. Then the last three weeks happened: 112.8, 138.4, 130.3, and a 24-9 all-play tied for the best in the league over that stretch. Ja'Marr Chase, Javonte Williams, C.J. Stroud — this thing projects 132 a week, 2nd of 12, off a draft that graded T-9th. The 79.0 in Week 6 is the ghost. Leif gets him Week 11 with 135 projected and no excuses left.

copies.headline: Grant Is Exactly What The Math Says
copies.body: Grant is 5-5, all-play 57-53, luck -0.2 — every number agrees he's a .500 team, which is almost impressive in its consistency. He averages 118.3 a game, 5th of 12, and projects for 119 next week, 6th of 12. The 148.5 last week was his second-best outing of the year behind the 158.6 in Week 7, and it came off 112.6 and 116.2, so temper it. His draft-night roster graded 80, T-9th of 12, and he's outrun that. Mahomes and Amon-Ra are real. The Week 3 84.4 was not.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Roster Finally Caught Up To Mitchell
copies.body: Three weeks ago this was a 1-7 corpse. Now Mitchell has put up 108.5, 128.6 and 149.0 — a 21-12 all-play over that stretch, 4th of 12 — and the record reads 3-7 anyway. That's what 1301.5 points against will do to a man; only one team in the league has absorbed more. Luck sits at -1.4 wins, so no, he's not imagining it. Gibbs and Nico Collins are doing real work and the roster projects 126 a week, 5th of 12. The season's over. The team isn't.

copies.headline: CJ Is 5-5 And Nobody's Impressed
copies.body: CJ won last week and stayed at 8, which tells you how much the win was worth. The 5-5 record is held together by a +0.6 luck cushion and the 5th-fewest points against in the league; the all-play is 48-62, and over the last three weeks it's 10-23 while he put up 95.1, 107.3 and 118.3. That's not a slump, that's the ceiling. Tyler Shough at quarterback is a choice. Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard keep him breathing, and 121 projected against Peter is at least a live week.

copies.headline: 7-3 Built On Sixty-Four Point Nightmares
copies.body: Leif is 7-3 and the all-play says 52-58. Both things are true, which is the whole problem. He's +2.3 wins over expected, 2nd-luckiest of 12, and has allowed the 2nd-fewest points in the league — that's a schedule, not a résumé. The last three weeks: 64.7, 95.2, 129.4, a 30% all-play stretch that ties for 10th. The roster index is 23 and the lineup projects 103 against Isaac. Josh Allen and Christian McCaffrey are carrying real weight; Kyle Pitts is projected for zero. The record will catch up eventually.

copies.headline: Best Draft In The League, Tenth-Best Scoring
copies.body: Peter drafted at an 89 out of 100, first of twelve on draft night, and has turned it into 1111.0 points, 9th of 12, with a 45-65 all-play that says 5-5 is generous. It is: luck is +0.9 wins, third-luckiest, and the L3 streak is the bill coming due. Last three weeks: 118.1, 93.9, 118.0, a 36% all-play. Bijan Robinson and A.J. Brown both project for zero, Brock Bowers is questionable, and Week 11 projects 86 against CJ. The career PF leader is scoring like a tenth-place team.

copies.headline: 6-4 And The Numbers Hate It
copies.body: Kaleb is 6-4 and nothing about that record is earned. He averages 103.2 a game, 12th of 12, his all-play is 40-70, and he's +2.4 wins over expected — the luckiest mark in the league. The 1,033.9 points against, fewest of 12, is the whole story. Weeks 8 and 9 were 62.7 and 76.8; the last three weeks all-play out at 6-27. The 127.4 bounceback is nice, but a draft that graded T-4th at 86 has decayed into a roster projecting 96 a week, 12th of 12. Adam's next.

copies.headline: The Postseason Assassin Runs Out Of Bullets
copies.body: Noah's whole brand is January, which is a problem when you're 3-7 and the all-play says 37-73, dead last at 34%. The 143.1 in Week 8 was fun; following it with 109.4 and 91.4 is the actual team. And luck isn't the alibi — minus 0.4 wins, basically fair, with the 3rd-fewest points against in the league. He drafted fine, 86 out of 100, T-4th. Then James Cook III and Garrett Wilson got surrounded by a roster projecting 100 a week. Week 11 against Logan is a dress-fitting appointment.

intro: Adam sits at the top with a 69.2 and he's earned every point of it — 139.4 a game, a 71% all-play mark nobody else is within seven points of, and a 7-3 record that luck had almost nothing to do with at -0.1. The bottom is a photo finish nobody wants to win: Kaleb's 31.9 edges Noah's 31.6 by three tenths, but Kaleb is 6-4 on +2.4 of luck and an 18% form reading, which is the kind of 6-4 that gets autopsied later. Mitchell is the climb worth noting, up from ninth to seventh at 3-7 despite -1.4 luck and a 64% form number — his 113.3 per game has been landing in the wrong matchups all year. Meanwhile Leif slid 7th to 9th and is 7-3 with +2.3 luck, 30% form and a 103 projection, which is a lot of ways of saying the same thing.
